checkpoints.description: [1/4] Add a cockpit SUPPLY LOCKER in the SHIP tab that buys and uses the station consumables

impact_assessment.why: The engine, REST and CLI can buy and use station consumables and /api/state now carries catalog_items, but the cockpit had no way to buy or use any of the four items, so a player taking hull damage in deep space could not apply the repair paste without leaving the UI
impact_assessment.benefits: Cockpit parity with the terminal; the four consumables are discoverable with price, held count and effect; BUY and USE never lie about their gates
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none (new additive panel); dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none (renders from snapshot)
impact_assessment.mitigation: bounded UI task with fast+snapshot proofs, real Edge DOM measurements at 1366x768 and 1280x720, ui_browser and ui_audit clean, full suite and 5/5 gates

impact_assessment.why: The supply locker can now sell and use the evasion decoy, and the engine allows use_item during combat, but the combat card offers only FIRE/ABSORB/EVADE/FLEE; when fuel is below 8 the flee button is disabled and the only escape is hidden behind the SHIP tab's supply disclosure
impact_assessment.benefits: The decoy is usable where the threat is, the low-fuel flee tooltip points at it, and the four consumables become a coherent loop: buy at a dock, use in context
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none (uses the existing /api/inventory/use route); dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none (reads ship.cargo)

checkpoints.description: [1/4] Let the captain buy a decoy and use it when fuel cannot buy an escape

impact_assessment.why: ADR-362's combat policy can only leave a fight with fuel: flee needs 8, evasive burn needs 3. With less than 3 fuel the captain fires until it dies even though ADR-370 made a held ECM decoy a guaranteed escape, and the supply run only ever buys a repair paste
impact_assessment.benefits: The full decoy loop (buy at a dock, deploy in a doomed fight) is exercised headlessly; fewer insurance rebuilds; the evade_combat effect is covered without manual UI play
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: one purchase and one use per encounter in page memory
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first unit tests for the purchase order and the last-resort branch, a scripted doomed-fight HTTP probe, three-seed campaigns, unchanged 180-step gate, full suite and 5/5 gates

checkpoints.description: [1/4] Show which anomaly power checks pass and make the captain pick a passing one

impact_assessment.why: Anomaly choices render only 'CHECK: SENSORS >= 45%' with no current effective power, so a player cannot tell a safe pick from a 15-hull failure; the AI captain always takes choices[0], which in campaign probes failed repeatedly (SENSORS 25% < 55%, SHIELDS 25% < 35%) and drove insurance rebuilds
impact_assessment.benefits: Encounter actions carry READY/FAILS with the effective percentage computed from the same engine formula; the cockpit shows it without markup changes; the captain resolves anomalies without needless hull loss and exercises non-first choices
impact_assessment.risks: contract: encounter anomaly actions gain ready + longer detail (additive); dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first payload and policy tests, Edge measurement of the rendered card at two viewports, three-seed campaigns, unchanged 180-step gate, full suite and 5/5 gates
